entrypoints.summary: The caller-controlled query string reaches GET /search; when Chrome has an authenticated session, the handler searches only that user's note bodies.
The supplied Android app launches Chrome Custom Tab navigations to /search?query=<known-prefix+candidate>.
The challenge evaluator logs Chrome into the admin account before installing and starting the submitted APK.

affected_components.role: Scopes search to the authenticated user's notes, renders search results, and sets the documented cookie and anti-framing headers.
Launches candidate search URLs, times Custom Tab navigation events, and chooses the maximum-duration candidate.

causal_paths.kind: attacker-controlled query to authenticated search result rendering
navigation event callbacks to candidate selection

code_slices.surrounding_context: The server configures SameSite=Lax and HttpOnly session cookies and emits X-Frame-Options: DENY plus CSP frame-ancestors 'none'; organizer documentation explains these framing controls do not stop top-level Custom Tab timing observation.
code_slices.vulnerable: The Flask search handler applies query as a LIKE pattern to current_user notes and renders search.html with a base64-encoded image value; the supplied solution states that a successful result embeds the large image while an unsuccessful result does not.

negative_controls: Other candidates in the same displayed pass have materially shorter recorded durations.
The organizer writeup states unsuccessful searches do not include the large base64-embedded image.
observability.positive_marker: A candidate has a markedly larger callback duration and is logged as max; the supplied trace records u=565 and Current flag: dice{l0lcu.

sources.concept: untrusted Android application controlling Custom Tab navigations

impact.affected_asset: Administrator note content, specifically the challenge flag.
impact.attacker_capability: A submitted Android application can recover one secret character at a time by selecting the candidate with the greatest navigation duration.
impact.security_effect: Cross-origin inference and iterative disclosure of the flag stored in the authenticated administrator's note.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled Android APK supplies successive candidate-prefix values in top-level Custom Tab navigations to the notes application's search endpoint after Chrome has been logged into the admin account.

Chrome's authenticated cookies are reused by the Custom Tab, while the untrusted app receives navigation start and finish callbacks; frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options do not block this top-level mobile navigation path.

The search handler applies the attacker-controlled query as a SQL LIKE pattern against the authenticated user's note bodies and renders the search response. Per the organizer writeup, a successful candidate produces a page with a large base64-encoded embedded image whereas an unsuccessful one does not.
The attacker app measures callback duration for each candidate, chooses the longest timing, and repeats to infer protected flag characters without reading browser cookies or page contents.

failure.operation: Custom Tab navigation timing distinguishes authenticated /search match and non-match responses.

primary_invariant.statement: An untrusted native caller must not be able to distinguish whether an authenticated user's protected note search matched from signals exposed by top-level browser navigation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The protected-search result changes the response's embedded-image behavior, and Custom Tabs exposes navigation-duration signals to the caller even though the caller cannot frame or directly read the protected page.

raw_refs.role: execution log of supplied attacker APK

quality.review_notes: Organizer writeup, vulnerable server source, attacker-app source, challenge runtime instructions, and a supplied logcat mutually corroborate the designed challenge mechanism. The log contains a concrete timing outlier (u=565 versus mostly roughly 39–57 ms) and selects that character. No server, browser, or Android remediation patch is supplied; mitigation is therefore a stated security-property recommendation, not an implemented fix. This is CTF-environment evidence and does not itself establish production-version scope.

remediation.invariant_restored: For attacker-selected searches, protected match and non-match state must not yield distinguishable navigation signals to an untrusted Custom Tab caller; framing headers alone do not restore this property on the documented top-level navigation path.
mitigation_classes: restriction of untrusted Custom Tab navigation/engagement signals for authenticated sensitive routes

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied evaluator starts a stock Google API 35 emulator, deploys a fresh app with an admin account, logs Chrome into that account, installs the attacker APK, then starts its MainActivity.
data_structure_invariants: The search query is only evaluated against Note.body records owned by current_user.
The attacker app maps each candidate character to a NAVIGATION_STARTED-to-NAVIGATION_FINISHED duration.
The recovered prefix is extended only with the maximum observed timing after an alphabet pass.

oracle.expected_positive: For a candidate extending the true prefix, its measured navigation duration is an outlier/maximum among the tested alphabet candidates.
